issues.description: The problem statement specifies a SealSaloon method named checkOrderReady(), but the reference implementation defines the corresponding behavior in a method named processOrders(). This identifier mismatch (checkOrderReady vs. processOrders) can confuse students about the exact method they must implement and prevents direct mapping between the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent between specification and implementation. Either rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady() and update its call sites (e.g., from orderMeal), or update the problem statement to require processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), so students have a clear, consistent method name to implement.
